name: fairy colors

attributes.attribute: worn as caps by fairy men
worn by fairy men and women
seen as unlucky by Highland women

sources: MacGregor, Alasdair Alpin. The Peat-Fire Flame: Folk-Tales and Traditions of the Highlands & Islands. Edinburgh: The Moray Press, 1937, 4.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy colors is a folkloric motif. Two hues, red and green, most often graced the fairy folk. Fairy men dressed in red caps and used green or blue breeches. Their women wore green dresses. Fairies took umbrage when humans wore these shades and could cause those people trouble. A century ago many Highland women turned down green as unlucky. Dundee's defeat at Killiecrankie was pinned on his wearing green that day. The lone fairies at times donned gray, as though to mark themselves off from the trooping kin.

okr.objective: Fairy colors is a folkloric motif tying red and green to the fairy folk.
key_results: Red and green were the fairy colors.
Fairy men wore red caps and green breeches.
